extracted.intended_audience: film and media scholars, students, and enthusiasts of Raymond Chandler, detective fiction, and film noir
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative focus on Raymond Chandler's fiction and screenwriting and their influence on film noir; includes criteria for literary qualities (tone, character, sense of place) and for scholarly treatment (research, analysis, readability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevation from pulp to literature
rubrics_metrics.description: More than any other writer, Raymond Chandler ... is responsible for raising detective stories from the level of pulp fiction to literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality detective fiction should transcend formulaic pulp plotting through literary prose, thematic depth, and stylistic distinction; evaluate on whether language and treatment lift the genre into serious literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard-boiled private-eye characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Chandler’s hard-boiled private eye Philip Marlowe set the standard for rough, brooding heroes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess protagonists for the archetypal traits Chandler exemplified: world-weariness, toughness, sardonic wit, and an interior brooding quality that grounds action in character psychology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral conviction at story's center
rubrics_metrics.description: who managed to maintain a strong sense of moral conviction despite a cruel and indifferent world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong detective fiction often posits a moral core in its lead despite pervasive corruption; evaluate how clearly the protagonist's ethics guide choices and contrast with the surrounding moral ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pessimism and grim realism (tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chandler’s seven novels ... with their pessimism and grim realism, had a direct influence on the emergence of film noir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge tone for sustained realism and pessimistic worldview—whether narrative voice, plot outcomes, and atmosphere convey gritty, unromanticized social environments linked to noir aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of place / evocation of setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Chandler worked to give his crime novels the flavor of his adopted city, Los Angeles, which was still something of a frontier town, rife with corruption and lawlessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how effectively prose evokes setting—local color, social texture, and environmental detail should feel integral to plot and character, shaping mood and plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence and suitability for cinematic adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Chandler’s ... novels ... had a direct influence on the emergence of film noir. In addition to novels, Chandler wrote short stories and penned the screenplays for several films, including Double Indemnity ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing adaptation potential, consider narrative economy, visual imagination, dialogue suitability, and thematic elements that translate to film noir; also consider the author's direct contributions to screenwriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of screenplay and collaboration dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: His work with Billy Wilder and Alfred Hitchcock on these projects was fraught with the difficulties of collaboration between established directors and an author who disliked having to edit his writing on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate screenplays not only on text but on collaborative history and adaptability—assess how well a screenplay survives/directorial changes, and whether it balances authorial voice with film production realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly thoroughness and archival research
rubrics_metrics.description: Creatures of Darkness is the first major biocritical study of Chandler in twenty years. Gene Phillips explores Chandler’s unpublished script for Lady in the Lake , examines the process of adaptation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good scholarship should demonstrate exhaustive research (use of unpublished scripts, interviews, archival materials), fill gaps left by prior commentators, and situate primary texts in historical and production contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical precision, readability, and accessibility in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Phillips constantly dazzles with both the precision of his presentation and the power of his analysis. ... Film noir and hard-boiled detective fiction enthusiasts of all levels of knowledge will find the book not only captivating, informative, and accessible, but a pure, page-turning delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical work should balance rigorous analysis with clear, engaging prose—precision of argument, power of insight, and accessibility to both specialists and general readers are important evaluative dimensions.
